title: Transfers T3: integrity on the server (no row lost on unlink, mirror adoption, complete links on repeat/restore/copy, no category on on-budget pairs)
description: Plan .agents/plans/2026-11-24_transfers-refactor.md, task T3. Map: transfers-map-api.md on the epic budget-e67y (point 8: R1, R2, R4, R5, R6). R1: editing the payee of one leg of a matcher-linked transfer to a normal payee, or deleting that leg, must restore the other bank-imported leg to what it was (as /transfers/unlink does via transfer_links.prev_*), never soft-delete it; later syncs must still see its bank id. R2: when the bank later imports the other side of a hand-made transfer, the matcher adopts the hand-made mirror instead of leaving two rows. R4/R5: repeat rules, restore and budget copy write both pointers and the transfer payee. Category is forced null on an on-budget pair on every write path.
notes:
Carry-overs from the budget-upgg reviews (review-upgg-3.md on budget-upgg): (2) absorb in the repair drops the folded payee's name and former names: record them on the kept payee so a stale edit after a repair cannot move a mirror; (3) a transfer row edited to rule text that produces an ordinary 'Transfer : X' payee stays a transfer (edited-payee.ts:63-66); (4) bulk import and bank sync rows that resolve to a transfer payee get the payee but NO mirror and no link (same as main): in scope here, they must become complete transfers or go through the matcher; (5) a kept unlinked payee keeps its transfer_rule; pre-existing: ensureTransferPayee uses an inconsistent pointer as-is, so insertMirror can use another account's payee and deleting the older of two same-named accounts can retire the newer one's payee.
